newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK Telecom calls C&W story "gossip".
newsitem.headline: HK Telecom calls C&W story "gossip".

text.p: A report in a British newspaper which said Britain's Cable and Wireless Plc planned to cut its stake in its subsidiary Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd was described by HK Telecom officials on Monday as speculation.
"This is gossip. It is pure speculation. You will have to ask Cable & Wireless," David Prince, HK Telecom's financial director said.
A spokeswoman for Hong Kong Telecoms said: "I don't think we are going to comment at this stage."

The report in London's Sunday Telegraph said Cable and Wireless Plc was set to reduce its stake in its subsidiary Hongkong Telecom to below 50 percent in return for better access to the Chinese telecoms market.
The newspaper said C&W chief executive, Dick Brown, was understood to have negotiated a deal with China as a trade-off, which was likely to result in Hongkong Telecom passing into Chinese hands.
Cable and Wireless could raise about one billion pounds ($1.65 billion) by cutting its 58.6 percent stake, valued at 12 billion stg, to 49.9 percent, the paper said.
